title: Sandbar: KV sampler weekly vignettes
content:
Week: 2029-03-11 to 2029-03-15
Owners / Attendees: Liam Chen (author), Aisha Patel, Rohan Gupta, Maya Alvarez, on-call rotation: eng-sre (Mar 11-15)

TL;DR
- Continued stabilization of the Sandbar KV sampler: reduced sampling-induced batch jitter by ~18% in internal canary.
- Kernel handshake patch (PR 897) merged to address race on slot reclamation; metrics look nominal in staging but still watching p99 CPU spikes on heavy multi-tenant runs.
- Nighttime drift incident on Wed 03/13 surfaced a scenario where sampler bias + small cohort sizes amplified latency — mitigation deployed (dynamic reservoir floor).
- Next week focus: finalize deterministic seeding experiment, extend sampler telemetry, and roll improved scheduler to two more islands.

Highlights and quick notes
- Reservoir floor mitigation: After the Wed incident we pushed a short-lived hotfix that prevents reservoir size from falling below 16 for cohorts with >10 concurrent sessions. Early numbers: median latency unchanged, p95 down ~6% for those cohorts. Ticket: SRV-4821.
- PR merged: github:repo/serving-runtime/pull/897 — handshake: guard against double-free of slot when prefill and eviction collide. Patch adds an epoch tag to slot metadata and a defensive check in the dealloc path. No functional regression in unit tests; integration traces show one less OOM-retry on the sample island.
- Canary results: running the improved sampler + handshake patch on canary cluster sandbar-02 for 48h. Token throughput is steady; observed microbatch interarrival STDDEV decreased by 18% versus baseline. Will keep canary live for another 72h to gather tail stats under synthetic multi-customer load.

Deep dives
1) Sampler bias & cohort fragmentation (notes from Rohan)\- Problem: when cohort sizes are small (<25 requests/min) and the sampler reservoir adapts downward aggressively, rare long-context requests become under-sampled and cause microbatches to spike.\- Reproduction: synthetic harness seeded with a 1:200 ratio of long-to-short requests produced consistent p99 spikes matching production incidents.\- Hypothesis verified: reservoir adaptation algorithm overshoots when variance in request sizes is high; the feedback loop length is too short (5s window).\- Short-term mitigation: reservoir_floor= max(16, min_configured), feedback_window extended to 20s for stable cohorts.\- Next steps: implement variance-aware adaptation (model reservoir step size by variance of recent sequence lengths).

2) Kernel handshake patch implications (notes from Aisha)\- Observed behaviour: slot reclamation racing with prefill path produced intermittent p99 CPU spikes and occasional failed prefill attempts.\- What we changed: introduced epoch tags and idempotent dealloc semantics; prefill now checks epoch before claiming a slot.\- Risk: small increase in slot retention time during pathological churn; mitigated by eviction backpressure which we tuned down slightly (eviction_threshold -2).\- Monitoring: added a histogram for slot retention-time and an alert if retention > 95th percentile baseline by 50%.

Operational incident summary (Wed 03/13, 02:30-03:12 UTC)\- Impact: ~3% of requests to region sandbar-us-east saw elevated p99 (peak +420ms) for ~42 minutes. No customer-facing errors.\- Root cause: sampler reservoir contracted rapidly on a small cohort after a traffic dip; a burst of long-context requests then caused a flurry of microbatches with unusually high prefill contention leading to local queueing. The handshake race exacerbated the tail.\- Mitigation steps taken:\  1) Raised reservoir floor for affected cohorts (immediate config push).\ 2) Rolled forward handshake patch to sandbar-02.\ 3) Rebalanced traffic away from sandbar-us-east island to sandbar-us-west for 20 minutes to let queues drain.\- Follow-ups: refine reservoir adaptation (SRV-4821), add synthetic tests for bursty long-context patterns, and run a chaos script to simulate prefill/evict races.

Experiments in flight
- Deterministic seeding experiment (Maya): aim to have sampler deterministic for A/B comparison. Status: seed hashing function landed in branch; results are mixed — variance in token-level runtimes reduced but sample diversity lowered slightly. Need an A/B run on non-cold traffic next week. Linked: github:repo/serving-runtime/pull/903 (WIP).\- Adaptive batching thresholding: small tweak to batch join timeout based on sliding-window variance. Early canary shows better p50 with little cost to throughput.
- Shadow sampler telemetry: added per-cohort sampled_fraction, reservoir_size, and sample_age histograms to the shadow pipeline; parsing rules updated in observability ingestion.

Open questions / decisions to make
- Deterministic seeding tradeoffs: if deterministic seeding reduces sample diversity, do we accept potential quality drift for improved reproducibility in experiments? Decision needed before wide rollout.
- Reservoir baseline policy: should default floor be 16 globally or be tiered by customer SLA/throughput class? Proposal: floor = 8 for best-effort, 16 for standard, 32 for premium.
- Handshake backoff: current short backoff reduces latency but increases slot retention under churn. Need to pick stable default after 1 week of canary data.

Action items (owner, ETA)
- Rohan: implement variance-aware reservoir adaptation prototype -> 2029-03-22 (SRV-4847).\- Maya: run A/B with deterministic seeding on non-cold traffic (canary islands sandbar-02 / sandbar-05) -> start 2029-03-18, report 2029-03-25.
- Aisha: extend sampler telemetry retention to 60 days and add alert thresholds for sample_age > 95p baseline -> 2029-03-19.
- Liam: coordinate chaos test for prefill/evict race on staging -> 2029-03-20 (github:repo/serving-runtime/actions/chaos-prefill).

Miscellaneous notes / meeting bits
- Quick sync outcome: infra team will prototype a low-cost synthetic harness to exercise long-context burst patterns (SRV-4860).\- Product asked for a short write-up on user impact framing for the reservoir floor change; Maya to draft one-pager by 03/20.
- Ops reminder: remember to stagger config pushes across islands to avoid correlated churn; doc link: confluence:serving-runtime/deploy-runbook.

Next sync: Fri 2029-03-22, 10:30 PT (standup deep-dive on reservoir adaptation).

Appendix: helpful traces and dashboards\- Canary dashboard: grafana/sandbar-sampler-canary (added slot retention histogram)\- Trace sample IDs: trace:ea3f-8cbb-1a2b (incident 03/13), trace:be2d-4f99-7c3d (post-fix confirmation)

Notes to self (short)\- Keep canary up until 03/18 to gather tail stats.\- If deterministic seeding reduces diversity by >5% on eval prompts, revert and iterate.
